_README: A retrieval test set for the advisory corpus, written by hand against
articles that are actually indexed.
Every `expect` string is matched case-insensitively against the title of
the retrieved passage's article. It is a substring rather than an exact
title because several articles cover a crop and any of them answering
is a pass -- what is being measured is whether the right subject came
back, not whether one particular page did.
The `off_topic` questions have no correct answer. For those the only
pass is an abstention, and that half of the set matters more than the
first: a retriever that answers everything scores well on recall and is
dangerous, because the citation it attaches makes a wrong answer look
checked.
Written by the team, not collected from farmers. A field-collected set
is what this should eventually be replaced with, and until then the
numbers say the system finds what we thought to ask it for.
The `exact_token` questions name a variety code or a molecule. They are
kept separate because they are the only case BM25 is for -- a code is
either in the passage or it is not, and an embedding that has learned
PBW 343 and HD 2967 are both wheat things will return whichever it
likes. The first version of this file had none of them, which made the
hybrid-versus-dense comparison meaningless: it measured hybrid on
exactly the questions where BM25 has nothing to add.
